name: The Roving Rookery
summary: With the Fallen gone, the postmaster makes her move: a murder pinned on the party, a village gone mad, and a dovecote that walks.

stages.journal: Geneva Fairchild came running with a white face: Theodora is dead in the post office, and the constable will blame the first stranger she sees.
stages.hint: Go with Geneva to the post office and look at the body.

stages.journal: Theodora was never a woman at all: the party named the postmaster, and she left her skin behind and her dovecote walked off over the roofs. Whatever she planned, it will not wait.
stages.hint: Watch the post, and watch the road. The valley will turn on you the moment the last of the Fallen is gone.

stages.journal: In the post office lie Theodora Mayville's skin and boneless remains. Geneva hangs back by the door, very quiet.
stages.hint: Look at the body, and look hard at Geneva.

stages.journal: 'Geneva' shrieked murder, burst into feathers and left an empty skin on the boards. Out the north window the dovecote stood up on pigeon legs and walked away. Now a posse is at the door with a forged letter.
stages.hint: Deal with the posse at the post office door: talk, run, give up, or fight.

stages.journal: We woke in the constable's cells, our gear locked away. The trial is at the next Witching Hour, and the mob is already chanting under the window.
objectives: Escape the cell before the trial
stages.hint: Get out of the cell before the Witching Hour: there are six ways, and most need no roll.

stages.journal: Wickermoor is hostile to its bones. Doors are barred, shops shuttered, mobs walk the lanes, and every roof is grey with pigeons. The charm will not lift until Golub is dead.
stages.hint: Find where the dovecote has settled. Look at the sky from the estate road, ask Hilda, or question Albert.

stages.journal: Golub's dovecote moves between four roosts, three nights from town, and it takes wing when Albert spots us. Every night it stays, the village tears itself further apart.
stages.hint: Reach a roost without Albert seeing: watch the pigeons' flight, read the tracks, or walk the circuit.

stages.journal: We are inside the walking dovecote. Parcels and pigeons below; Golub's roost above.
stages.hint: Climb to the roost floor and end Golub.

stages.journal: Golub Graygullet is dead and the dovecote has settled for good. The charm broke like a held breath, and Wickermoor woke up dazed and ashamed.
